name: Escitalopram
metabolism: CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 mediate N-demethylation to S-demethylcitalopram, followed by further demethylation. The metabolites have weaker serotonin-reuptake effects; some parent and metabolites are eliminated in urine.
summary: Escitalopram is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) antidepressant used to treat major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and social anxiety disorder.
toxicities: DailyMed warnings include suicidal thoughts/behavior, serotonin syndrome, discontinuation syndrome, seizures, mania/hypomania, hyponatremia, bleeding, cognitive/motor impairment, and angle-closure glaucoma in susceptible patients.
Common adverse reactions include insomnia, nausea, sweating, fatigue, somnolence, decreased libido, and sexual dysfunction.
generalRisks: The label is for prescription oral escitalopram tablets (revised 2026-05). About suicidality, serotonin syndrome, discontinuation symptoms, seizures, mania/hypomania, hyponatremia, bleeding and impaired cognitive/motor performance. MAOIs and pimozide are contraindicated; label dosage guidance is not a recreational-use reference.
saferUse: Monitor for worsening mood or suicidal thoughts, particularly in younger patients and after treatment changes. Seek urgent care for suspected serotonin syndrome or seizure.
Do not stop abruptly; the label advises gradual dose reduction and monitoring for discontinuation symptoms. Use caution with driving or machinery if impaired.
Do not combine with MAOIs or pimozide. Check before combining with serotonergic medicines, NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin, or other anticoagulants.
dosageRemark: The label is a prescription oral tablet label. Therapeutic dosing is not recreational dose guidance; no recreational threshold or duration is established here.
